received_message: Hi Daniel. I want to talk about what happened with Aram's homework last night. I was upset by how loud things got, and by the word "lazy". I also know I told you that you were overreacting in front of Aram, and then let him keep the tablet. I think that made it harder for you. I'd like us to be on the same side with him. I'd like us to agree on rules for homework and screens together, so neither of us has to decide alone. How did the evening look from your side? I'd like to hear it.

summary.title: Disagreement with Leila over Aram's homework
summary.what_happened: Aram has skipped homework three times this week, and his teacher emailed us about it. Last night I raised my voice and used the word lazy, which I now regret. Leila told me I was overreacting in front of him, and then let him keep the tablet.
summary.my_feelings: I regret the word I used. I feel my rules are not taken seriously when they are changed in front of Aram.
summary.my_needs: I need us to back each other's decisions in front of Aram, and to talk about rules between ourselves.
summary.desired_outcome: I want us to work as a team. I am willing to be calmer if my decisions are not cancelled in front of him.

perspective_summary: This person is concerned about how loud and harsh the evening became and about being called overreacting in front of the child. They feel the child's rules lose weight when a decision made by one parent is reversed in front of him. They accept that the tone and one word used were wrong. They want both parents to be calm and to agree on homework and consequences together.

consult.text:
It sounds like you were worried and frustrated. Aram has skipped homework three times, the teacher has written, and then your decision was reversed in front of him. That would feel like being undermined.

Leila has written to you, and she seems to see it differently in one way. She was upset by the shouting and the word lazy, and she wants you both to set rules together. She also says that telling you that you were overreacting in front of Aram, and letting him keep the tablet, was not helpful. That is a real opening. She is not only criticising you.

One thing that may have made this harder is how the evening went. You have said yourself that raising your voice and the word lazy were wrong, and that matters. A two-week ban decided in the moment may also have been hard for her to support, since the two of you had not agreed on it first.

We do not know yet how Aram felt, or what Leila would call a fair consequence.

Some next steps. First, reply to Leila and say that you regret the word, which is honest and sets a calm tone. Second, suggest sitting down without Aram to agree on homework rules and what happens when they are not followed. Third, agree that when you disagree, you will talk privately first.
